## Observed Facts
- Data Scope: BGL, full range (2005-06-03 to 2006-01-04 [E2]), filter level = FATAL. There are 855,195 FATAL Log Entries in total [E1].
- FATAL Log Entries by Component [E1]:
  - KERNEL: 626,450
  - APP: 228,536
  - LINKCARD: 206
  - MMCS: 3
- KERNEL and APP together account for nearly all FATAL Log Entries. These are Log Entry counts, not incident counts.
- The tools returned no field that maps a Component to a Team. The BGL columns are only alert_tag, component, level and node [E2].

## Hypotheses
- I can't name the Teams, but KERNEL and APP are the Components to take to whoever owns the ownership mapping. Any Team that owns KERNEL would hold most of the FATAL volume. That is a guess about volume, not a fact about ownership.
- The FATAL volume may come from a few repeated messages or bursts, so the Log Entry counts could overstate how many distinct problems there are. I haven't tested this.

## Unknowns
- Which Team owns KERNEL, APP, LINKCARD or MMCS. The logs don't record ownership, and I won't guess.
- Whether the KERNEL and APP FATAL counts come from sustained recurrence or a few bursts. I haven't run a trend yet.

## Next Step
- Send the Component ranking above (KERNEL, then APP) to whoever keeps the Component-to-Team mapping, such as a service catalog or CODEOWNERS file, to identify the Teams.
- Meanwhile I can run a monthly trend of FATAL Log Entries for KERNEL and APP, and group them by alert_tag or message. That would show whether they recur steadily or come in bursts, and which problem to investigate first.
